objective: Test whether suppressing duplicate full-prefix checkpoint creation after an exact snapshot hit preserves cache lifecycle semantics and removes replay-time eviction without changing the 8 GiB production default.
hypothesis: Exact lookup already touches and pins the retained snapshot, so treating that logical full prefix as checkpointed will avoid a duplicate reservation, clone, and same-key store while preserving output, LRU, cleanup, miss, strict-prefix append, cancellation, and persistence behavior.
success_gates: Focused exact-hit tests fail before implementation and then prove zero duplicate reservation, clone, or store while preserving the existing lookup touch, pin, and terminal unpin.
Miss, strict-prefix append, cancellation, disabled-cache, persistence, and terminal cleanup controls retain their current behavior.

Fresh 4 GiB reruns for I080 offsets 6, 18, and 24 match the locked source/plan/execution and terminal identities, retain six snapshots, and record zero eviction, preflight skip, dropped trace event, or replay prefill.
Any failed gate rolls back the runtime change; a pass admits only a wider 8 GiB no-regression validation and cannot lower the production snapshot budget in I081.
next_actions: Add failing exact-hit lifecycle tests plus miss, strict-prefix, cancellation, LRU, pin/unpin, and persistence controls.

Run affected and full verification, then rerun only locked failing offsets 6, 18, and 24 at temporary 4 GiB in fresh processes.
